Hubble can see detail down to less than 0.1 arcsecond across.
An arcsecond is approximately the angle subtended by a U.S. dime coin (18 mm) at a distance of 4 kilometres (about 2.5 mi).

Hubble orbits the Earth about every 97 minutes at an altitude of about 353 miles (569 kilometers)..

Therefore, 0.1 arcsecond is the angle subtended by a dime at 40km or 25 miles, and at an orbital height of 353 miles would be more than 14 times larger, or 254 millimeters across, about 10 inches. So not even Hubble can read your license plate, let alone scratches on a wedding ring.
